title: Thriftline: Adaptive Serving Efficiency playbook for batching, caching, and quantization
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Objective: Build a repeatable program and playbook (Thriftline) that drives sustained unit-cost reduction across Redwood hosted and Dedicated deployments by combining adaptive batching, predictive KV/prefix caching, and targeted quantization profiles.

Hypothesis: We can reduce per-token infra spend by 15–25% for typical production workloads without degrading end-to-end application quality or violating p99 latency SLOs by: (1) applying adaptive batching tied to request latency budgets, (2) introducing predictive prefix/KV caching for frequent prompt families, and (3) rolling out conservative quantization profiles for non-critical model variants.

Scope: Hosted API and Dedicated pools initially; Private/VPC rollout deferred to Phase 2. Workstreams include metric & eval instrumentation, runtime batching strategy, cache eviction/policy design, quantization profiling, rollout automation, and customer comms/playbooks for model owners.

Primary OKRs: 
- OKR-1: Reduce hosted per-token compute cost by 20% (baseline Q4 2024) across top 10 customer workloads.
- OKR-2: Maintain p99 response latency within +5% of baseline for those workloads.
- OKR-3: Ship automation to gate quantization rollouts by eval regressions and rollback on quality alerts.

Stakeholders: Product (Sofia Chen), Runtime Eng (Marcus Lowe, ENG), Research/Applied ML (Dr. Aisha Rao), Console/Observability (Ethan Park), Solutions/Success (Lina Torres).
